summary: Follow-up part for layer RD.5 (finiteness, duality and Künneth for rigid cohomology). It plans what the first pass left as gaps or open targets: proper cohomological descent through Le Stum's overconvergent site and Zureick-Brown's proof (modifications, finite flat and fppf coverings, proper surjections, the descent spectral sequence, replacing the unread Tsuzuki 2003); Berthelot's trace morphism, the lemma on homomorphisms out of overconvergent germs (Dualité, Lemme 2.1), compact-support Gysin maps, finite étale traces, the duality morphism with its morphism of triangles and the Künneth pairings on product tubes (replacing the unread Tsuzuki 1999 and Berthelot's Dualité, now read from the author's copy), and base-field extension; the dimension 2g + d − 1 of H^1 of an affine curve from the Mayer–Vietoris sequences of a lifted curve and its boundary discs; Crew's nonarchimedean duality inputs (Fréchet and dual-of-Fréchet spaces, transposes of strict maps, residue duality of the Robba ring and its plus and minus parts), with Hahn–Banach imported from LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L0; unipotent monodromy along a boundary (docility), Kedlaya's extension theorem, dense-open full faithfulness and subquotient closure, convergent log-isocrystals, logarithmic extension and Kedlaya's semistable reduction theorem; the log-rigid comparison for curves and the finite-level Igusa finiteness of Pan, Proposition 5.1.7; finiteness for smooth quasi-projective integral models and their boundary strata (the RD.5 request of AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII:AG2.4); smooth proper direct images of convergent F-isocrystals (Shiho, Xu, Guo–Reinecke); and Kedlaya's finite projections étale off the hyperplane at infinity, the theorem behind the exported finite-étale affine-cover node.

nodes.title: Le Stum's overconvergent site of a variety
nodes.statement: Fix a complete discretely valued field K of characteristic 0 with ring of integers V and residue field k. An overconvergent variety over V is a triple (X ⊂ P ← V) of a k-variety X, a locally closed immersion of X into the special fibre of a formal V-scheme P (locally topologically of finite presentation) and a morphism λ: V → P_K of strictly K-analytic varieties; its tube is ]X[_V = λ^{-1}(sp^{-1}(X)). The category An†(V) is the localisation of the category of such triples (with formal morphisms) at strict neighbourhoods, i.e. morphisms are germs of analytic maps defined on a neighbourhood of the tube; it carries the analytic topology induced from coverings of the tubes. For a k-variety X (over an overconvergent base (C, O)), the overconvergent site An†(X/O) is the slice category of overconvergent varieties (Y ⊂ Q ← W) together with a morphism Y → X over C, with the induced topology; its good version An†_g(X/O) uses good analytic varieties. It is ringed by the sheaf O† of overconvergent functions, (Y, W) ↦ Γ(]Y[_W, i^{-1}O_W). An overconvergent crystal is an O†-module whose transition maps along all morphisms are isomorphisms; Mod†_{g,fp}(X/O) denotes the finitely presented O†-modules on the good site.
hypotheses: K of characteristic 0 (needed for the comparison with connections, Le Stum Theorem 3.5.9).

Analytic varieties are strictly K-analytic in Berkovich's sense; Le Stum's comparison theorem (RD.5/overconvergent-site-comparison) identifies the cohomology with Berthelot's rigid cohomology of RD.4, so the Berkovich formalism is not exported beyond this layer.
proofSteps: Formal embeddings and tubes: Le Stum §2.1 (Definition 2.1.2, Proposition 2.1.6: the tube functor is left exact).
Overconvergent varieties and the localisation at strict neighbourhoods: Definitions 2.2.1 and 2.3.7; the analytic topology: Definition 2.4.1.
The site of X: Definition 2.4.11 (X/O := j_!(X) as an overconvergent sheaf); good sites: Definition 2.5.13; a geometric realisation (X, V) of X over (C, O) is a covering of X/O (Proposition 2.5.14).
The ring O†: Definition 3.3.4; crystals: Definition 3.3.7; on a single overconvergent variety crystals are the i^{-1}O_V-modules on the tube (Proposition 3.3.8).
acceptance: For X = Spec k and P = Spf V, An†(X/V) has the final object (Spec k ⊂ Spf V ← M(K)) and O† on it is K.
For X = A^1_k with realisation (A^1 ⊂ P̂^1_V ← P^{1,an}_K), the sections of O† on that object are the overconvergent functions K⟨t⟩†.

nodes.title: Overconvergent isocrystals are crystals on the overconvergent site, with the same cohomology
nodes.statement: Let K have characteristic 0, S a good formal V-scheme and p: X → S_k a morphism of k-varieties. Then there is a canonical equivalence Mod†_{g,fp}(X/S) ≃ Isoc†(X/S) between finitely presented O†-modules on the good overconvergent site and overconvergent isocrystals, and for E ∈ Isoc†(X/S) one has (Rp_{rig*}E)^{an} = Rp_{X/S*}E. In particular, for S = Spf V and every i, H^i_rig(X/K, E) = H^i((X/V)_{An†_g}, E), compatibly with pullback along morphisms of varieties and with Frobenius pullback.
hypotheses: Char K = 0; good base (every point of the analytic base has an affinoid neighbourhood).
Isoc†(X/S) and H^i_rig are those of RD.3/overconvergent-isocrystals-of-a-variety and RD.4/rigid-cohomology (Berthelot's definition through frames and j†).
proofSteps: On a geometric realisation (X, V) (formal embedding proper and smooth at X), crystals are i^{-1}O_V-modules on ]X[_V with an overconvergent stratification, equivalently (char 0) coherent modules with an overconvergent integrable connection (Le Stum Theorem 3.5.9 via Propositions 3.5.3 and 3.5.6); this matches the frame description of Isoc† (RD.3/overconvergent-isocrystal-connection-form), independently of the realisation (Le Stum Proposition 3.5.11).

Cohomology: the push-forward to the realisation is computed by the de Rham complex of the connection on the tube (Le Stum Proposition 4.5.4 and the Poincaré lemma, Proposition 4.5.5); globalise by Zariski localisation for sheaves of Zariski type (Le Stum §4.6, Theorem 4.6.7), which gives Berthelot's j†-de Rham complex (RD.4/overconvergent-de-rham-complex).
Functoriality and Frobenius: both sides are functorial in X, and Frobenius pullback acts on crystals by the absolute Frobenius of X.
acceptance: For X = A^1_k and E = O, H^0 = K and H^1 = K⟨t⟩†dt / d(K⟨t⟩†) = 0 (every overconvergent series has an overconvergent antiderivative), as for rigid cohomology (RD.4/cohomology-of-affine-space).
For X = G_m, H^1 is spanned by dt/t on both sides (RD.4/cohomology-of-multiplicative-group).

nodes.title: Modifications are universally of cohomological descent for overconvergent crystals
nodes.statement: Let p: X → Y be a modification of k-varieties (proper, and an isomorphism over a dense open of Y). Then p, viewed as a morphism of sheaves on the overconvergent site over any overconvergent base, is universally of cohomological descent with respect to overconvergent crystals: for every base change Y' → Y and every crystal F on Y', F → Rp'_{•*}p'^{*}_•F is an isomorphism for the Čech hypercover of p'. The same holds for a locally finite Zariski covering, a covering by closed subschemes, and the map from the disjoint union of the reduced irreducible components.
hypotheses: k-varieties in Zureick-Brown's sense (locally of finite type, not necessarily separated or reduced).
Descent is with respect to crystals, not all abelian sheaves (Zureick-Brown Remark 1.2 explains why the étale template does not apply).
proofSteps: Zariski and closed coverings (Zureick-Brown Theorem 5.9): the coverings by open or closed pieces induce surjections on tubes; reduce to realisations, where descent holds for coverings of analytic spaces (Lemmas 5.4, 5.6), and conclude with the formal calculus of universal cohomological descent (Zureick-Brown Corollary 3.18, from EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2 as requested). Irreducible components: Corollary 5.12.

Blow-up along an ideal generated by two elements f, g (Zureick-Brown Lemma 5.14, after Tsuzuki 2004, Lemma 3.4.5): cover the tube by U_1 = ]Z[ and U_2 = {|f̂| > λ or |ĝ| > λ}; over U_1 the blow-up tube is P^1 × U_1 (a map with a section, Theorem 3.16 (ii), and Lemma 5.2 since the map of tubes is surjective), over U_2 the blow-up is an isomorphism of tubes; glue with Theorem 3.17 (c), (d).

General blow-ups reduce to two-generator ones by a sequence of blow-ups (Lemma 5.15, Tsuzuki's Lemma 3.4.4); a modification is dominated, by Chow's lemma, by a projective one, locally a blow-up (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4/chow-lemma, SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4/modification-domination); cancellation (Theorem 3.17 (b)) finishes (Zureick-Brown Proposition 5.16).
acceptance: The normalisation p: Ỹ = P^1 → Y of a nodal cubic is a modification; Ỹ ×_Y Ỹ is Ỹ together with the two points (y_1, y_2), (y_2, y_1) over the node, and the Čech descent spectral sequence of p produces from them the extra class of H^1_rig(Y), of dimension 1 while H^1_rig(Ỹ) = 0.
Degenerate case: an isomorphism is a modification whose Čech hypercovering is constant, and descent is the identity.

nodes.title: Finite flat and fppf coverings are universally of cohomological descent for finitely presented crystals
nodes.statement: (a) Let (f, u): (X', V') → (X, V) be a finite morphism of overconvergent varieties such that, after shrinking V and V', u is universally flat and surjective. Then (f, u) is universally of cohomological descent for finitely presented overconvergent crystals. (b) Every fppf covering p: X → Y of k-varieties (faithfully flat, locally of finite presentation) is universally of cohomological descent for finitely presented crystals on the overconvergent site.
hypotheses: Finitely presented crystals (realised as i^{-1} of coherent modules on a neighbourhood).
proofSteps: (a) By the Čech criterion it suffices to show R^q p_{i*}p_i^* F = 0 for q > 0 and exactness of the Čech complex; on realisations these are vanishing of higher direct images of coherent sheaves along finite maps of analytic spaces and fpqc descent for coherent sheaves in the flat quasi-finite topology (Zureick-Brown Proposition 5.19, using Berkovich 1993, Corollary 4.3.2 and Proposition 4.1.2).

(b) Step 0: refine an fppf covering by a composite of finite locally free surjections and Zariski coverings (Stacks 05WN) and reduce by Theorem 5.9 and Corollary 3.18. Step 1 (monogenic): embed and homogenise; flatten the projective homogenisation by a modification away from X (Raynaud–Gruson, SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4/flattening-by-blowup), obtaining a finite flat map of formal schemes, and apply (a). Step 2: a finite field extension is a tower of monogenic ones. Step 3: over the algebraic closure, finite locally free maps are locally monogenic (Bosch–Lütkebohmert–Raynaud §2.3 Proposition 3), descend to a finite extension of k (Zureick-Brown proof of Theorem 1.1 (i), pp. 22–24).
Remark: the modification in Step 1 is needed: a monogenic map can homogenise to a non-flat map (Zureick-Brown Remark 5.20).
acceptance: A purely inseparable extension k ⊂ k^{1/p} gives a monogenic finite flat covering Spec k^{1/p} → Spec k of cohomological descent, compatible with the invariance of rigid cohomology under nilpotent thickenings used in RD.5/smooth-proper-hypercovering.
The Kummer covering t ↦ t^ℓ of G_m (ℓ prime to p) is finite flat; descent recovers H^*_rig(G_m) from the Čech complex of the covering.

nodes.title: Proper surjections are universally of cohomological descent for finitely presented crystals
nodes.statement: Every proper surjective morphism p: X → Y of k-varieties is universally of cohomological descent for finitely presented crystals on the overconvergent site. Consequently every proper hypercovering Y_• → X (each Y_{n+1} → (cosk_n Y_•)_{n+1} proper surjective) is universally of cohomological descent for finitely presented crystals.
hypotheses: Finitely presented crystals; proper hypercoverings in the sense of SGA 4 Vbis (for P the class of proper surjections, stable under base change and composition).
proofSteps: Chow's lemma (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4/chow-lemma) and cancellation reduce to p projective; Zariski-locally on Y (RD.5/modification-cohomological-descent) assume Y affine.

Raynaud–Gruson flattening (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4/flattening-by-blowup) gives a modification Y' → Y whose strict transform X' → Y' is flat; X' → Y' is an fppf covering, hence of descent (RD.5/fppf-cohomological-descent (b)), and Y' → Y is a modification (RD.5/modification-cohomological-descent); compose (Zureick-Brown Theorem 3.17 (c)) and cancel to X → Y (3.17 (b)) (Zureick-Brown proof of Theorem 1.1 (ii), p. 24).

Hypercoverings: a P-hypercovering with P the class of morphisms universally of cohomological descent is itself universally of cohomological descent (Zureick-Brown Theorem 3.16 (iv), Conrad Theorem 7.10), requested from EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2.
acceptance: The normalisation of the cuspidal cubic is a proper surjection which is a universal homeomorphism; descent gives H^*_rig(cusp) ≅ H^*_rig(P^1) (rigid cohomology does not see the cusp).

For the blow-up Bl → A^2 at the origin with exceptional curve E ≅ P^1, descent along the proper surjection Bl ⊔ {0} → A^2 gives the abstract blow-up sequence … → H^i_rig(A^2) → H^i_rig(Bl) ⊕ H^i_rig(pt) → H^i_rig(E) → H^{i+1}_rig(A^2) → …, whence H^2_rig(Bl) ≅ H^2_rig(E) = K(−1).

sources.match: Proper surjections are universally of cohomological descent for finitely presented crystals, by Chow's lemma, Raynaud–Gruson flattening and the flat and modification cases.
Hypercoverings built from morphisms universally of cohomological descent are universally of cohomological descent (citing Conrad, Theorem 7.10).
The earlier proof of descent for étale-proper hypercoverings in Berthelot's framework, of which the proper case (Tsuzuki, Invent. Math. 151) is the continuation.

nodes.title: The descent spectral sequence of rigid cohomology for proper hypercoverings (Chiarellotto–Tsuzuki, Tsuzuki)
nodes.statement: Let X be a separated k-scheme of finite type, E ∈ F-Isoc†(X/K) and f_•: Y_• → X a proper hypercovering by separated k-schemes of finite type. Then there is a spectral sequence E_1^{q,r} = H^r_rig(Y_q/K, f_q^*E) ⇒ H^{q+r}_rig(X/K, E), functorial in E and in the hypercovering, and compatible with Frobenius (the Frobenius of E_1 being that of each H_rig(Y_q, f_q^*E)). For an étale hypercovering it is the spectral sequence of Chiarellotto–Tsuzuki, Theorem 11.7.1; for a proper hypercovering it is Tsuzuki's (Invent. Math. 151, Theorem 4.5.1), here obtained through the overconvergent site.
hypotheses: Overconvergent isocrystals are finitely presented crystals on the overconvergent site (RD.5/overconvergent-site-comparison).
No smoothness of the Y_q is required; RD.5/smooth-proper-hypercovering supplies Y_q smooth over purely inseparable extensions for the finiteness application.
proofSteps: By RD.5/proper-surjection-cohomological-descent, E → Rf_{•*}f_•^*E is an isomorphism on the overconvergent site of X.

Apply RΓ and the E_1 spectral sequence of an augmented simplicial topos (Zureick-Brown Remark 3.9, equation (3.9.3); EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2/hypercovers-and-cohomological-descent): E_1^{q,r} = H^r(Y_q, f_q^*E) ⇒ H^{q+r}(X, E).

Identify site cohomology with rigid cohomology termwise (RD.5/overconvergent-site-comparison, Le Stum Corollary 4.6.8); functoriality and Frobenius follow since Frobenius pullback is a morphism of hypercoverings over the absolute Frobenius of X.
acceptance: For the normalisation Ỹ → Y of a nodal curve with node y and preimages y_1, y_2, the hypercovering Ỹ ⊔ {y} → Y gives the exact sequence 0 → H^0(Y) → H^0(Ỹ) ⊕ K → K^2 → H^1(Y) → H^1(Ỹ) → 0.
For a Čech hypercovering of a Zariski open cover the spectral sequence is the Mayer–Vietoris spectral sequence.

nodes.title: Homomorphisms out of overconvergent germs are sections supported on the tube (Berthelot, Lemme 2.1)
nodes.statement: Let (X, Y, P) be a frame with X open in Y, Z = Y \ X, j: ]X[ ⊂ ]Y[ and Γ_{]X[} the functor of sections with support in ]X[ (the kernel of restriction to the open tube ]Z[). For sheaves E, F of K-vector spaces on ]Y[ there is a canonical isomorphism of sheaves Hom_K(j†E, F) ≅ Γ_{]X[}(Hom_K(E, F)), natural in E and F. Consequently every K-bilinear pairing of complexes E• ⊗_K F• → G• on ]Y[ induces a pairing j†E• ⊗_K Γ_{]X[}F• → Γ_{]X[}G•, compatible with restriction to smaller open X' ⊂ X.
hypotheses: Classical rigid (Tate) topology on ]Y[; ]Z[ is an admissible open and {V_λ, ]Z[} is an admissible covering of ]Y[ for every strict neighbourhood V_λ of ]X[ (RD.3/strict-neighbourhood).
j†E = colim_V j_{V*} j_V^{-1} E over strict neighbourhoods V of ]X[ (RD.3/j-dagger).
proofSteps: The restriction of j†E to ]Z[ vanishes: a quasi-compact admissible W ⊂ ]Z[ satisfies |f| ≤ η < 1 on W for the defining functions f, hence misses V_λ for λ > η, and (j†E)(W) = colim_λ E(W ∩ V_λ) = 0.
Map one way: a homomorphism ψ: j†E → F composed with the adjunction E → j†E is a homomorphism E → F whose restriction to ]Z[ is zero, i.e. a section of Γ_{]X[}Hom(E, F).

Map the other way: given φ: E → F vanishing on ]Z[, a germ s ∈ E(W ∩ V) on a quasi-compact W is sent to the section of F(W) obtained by gluing φ(s) on W ∩ V with 0 on W ∩ ]Z[, using the admissible covering {W ∩ V, W ∩ ]Z[} of W; the two agree on the overlap because φ vanishes on ]Z[. The constructions are inverse and natural.
For the pairing statement apply the isomorphism to the adjoint E• → Hom(F•, G•) and use Γ_{]X[}Hom(F, G) → Hom(Γ_{]X[}F, Γ_{]X[}G).
acceptance: For X = Y (no boundary) both sides are Hom_K(E, F).

For E = F = O on the frame A^1 ⊂ P^1, both sides have no nonzero global sections: a function on P^{1,an} vanishing on the open disc ]∞[ vanishes identically, so there is no nonzero map j†O → O (the natural map goes O → j†O).

sources.match: States the canonical isomorphism between homomorphisms out of j† of a sheaf and sections with support in the tube of the internal Hom, and deduces by adjunction the induced pairing of j† with Γ_{]X[}; the proof is said to be a direct verification.
Uses the induced pairing to construct cup products between rigid cohomology and compact-support cohomology with coefficients.

nodes.title: Berthelot's trace morphism on top-degree compact-support rigid cohomology
nodes.statement: For every separated k-scheme X of finite type and pure dimension n there is a K-linear trace Tr_X: H^{2n}_{c,rig}(X/K) → K, characterised as follows. If X is affine, smooth and geometrically connected, choose a smooth affine W-scheme X' lifting X and a projective compactification X̄' with structure map h: X̄'_K → Spec K; then Tr_X is induced by the composite H^n_{]X[}(X̄'^{an}_K, Ω^n) → H^0_{]X[}(X̄'^{an}_K, ω^{an}) → H^0(X̄'^{an}_K, ω^{an}) ≅ H^0(X̄'_K, ω) → K of the class map for the dualising complex ω = h^!K (equal to Ω^n[n] on the smooth locus X'_K), the forget-supports map, rigid GAGA and Grothendieck's trace; this composite kills the image of H^n_{]X[}(Ω^{n−1}), so it factors through H^{2n}_{c,rig}(X) = H^{2n}_{]X[}(X̄'^{an}_K, Ω^•), the quotient of H^n_{]X[}(Ω^n) by that image. In general Tr_X is obtained after a finite extension of k from an affine smooth geometrically connected open dense U with dim(X \ U) < n, using that H^{2n}_{c,rig}(U) → H^{2n}_{c,rig}(X) is surjective, and descended by the trace of the finite extension of K. Tr_X is independent of all choices, is Frobenius-equivariant as a map H^{2n}_{c,rig}(X/K) → K(−n), and is the trace Tr_X used by RD.5/trace-map.
hypotheses: Pure dimension n; for n = 0 the trace of a finite étale k-scheme is the sum of the field traces.
Constant coefficients; traces with coefficients are obtained by composing the cup product with the evaluation E ⊗ E^∨ → O (RD.5/poincare-pairing).
A Cohen ring W of k with fraction field K (for perfect k the Witt vectors), as in Berthelot's note.
proofSteps: Vanishing: H^d_{c,rig}(X) = 0 for d > 2n (RD.5/compact-support-vanishing-above-twice-dimension), so excision shows H^{2n}_{c,rig}(U) → H^{2n}_{c,rig}(X) is surjective for U open with dim(X \ U) < n (RD.4/excision-sequence).

Affine smooth case: the analytification X'^{an}_K of the affine lift is a strict neighbourhood of the tube of X in X̄'^{an}_K, and the compact-support complex of X is computed by RΓ_{]X[} of the de Rham complex (RD.4/compactly-supported-rigid-cohomology); compose with the class map of Ω^n[n] → ω, the GAGA isomorphism for the coherent complex ω, and Grothendieck's trace for the proper K-scheme X̄'_K.
The composite vanishes on the image of H^n_{]X[}(Ω^{n−1}): the trace kills exact top forms (Berthelot 1.2); hence the factorisation through H^{2n}_{c,rig}.

Independence of the compactification and invariance under shrinking X with fixed X̄' are immediate from the construction (Berthelot 1.2); independence of the lift X': by RD.5/top-degree-dimension-one the space H^{2n}_{c,rig}(X) is a line, and by RD.5/compact-support-gysin-and-trace the Gysin map of a W-section, which only depends on the formal completion, is inverse to the trace of each lift (Berthelot Proposition 1.6); independence of U follows by comparing two opens with their intersection.
Frobenius: the trace of a Frobenius lift multiplies the residue class of the top form by q^n (RD.4/frobenius-on-rigid-cohomology), so Tr is equivariant into K(−n) (RD.4/tate-twist).
acceptance: For X = Spec k, Tr_X is the identity of K.

For X = A^1, the class in H^2_{c,rig}(A^1) of the compactly supported form whose residue is 1 maps to 1 (RD.4/compactly-supported-cohomology-of-affine-space), so Tr_{A^1} is an isomorphism H^2_{c,rig}(A^1) ≅ K(−1).
For a finite étale map f: Y → X of degree d between smooth affines, Tr_X ∘ Tr_{f,c} = Tr_Y (Berthelot 1.7 (ii)).

sources.match: Constructs the trace by lifting a smooth affine geometrically connected X to a smooth affine W-scheme with projective compactification, using the dualising complex, GAGA on the analytic space, Grothendieck's trace (Hartshorne, Residues and Duality VII 3.4) and the vanishing on (n−1)-forms; reduces the general case to such an open after a finite extension of k.
Vanishing of compact-support cohomology above twice the dimension, used to pass to a dense open.
Independence of the lift.
Compatibility of the trace with the crystalline trace for proper smooth X and with finite étale traces.

the trace gives the target K(−n) of the Poincaré pairing with coefficients
the twist K(−n) of the trace fixes the normalisation of Frobenius weights in duality

api.name: rigidTrace
api.statement: Tr_X: H^{2n}_{c,rig}(X/K) → K for X of pure dimension n.

api.name: rigidTrace_frobenius
api.statement: Tr_X ∘ Φ = q^n · σ_K ∘ Tr_X, i.e. Tr_X is a morphism of F-spaces H^{2n}_{c,rig}(X/K) → K(−n).

api.name: rigidTrace_openImmersion
api.statement: For U ⊂ X open dense, Tr_U = Tr_X ∘ (extension by zero H^{2n}_{c,rig}(U) → H^{2n}_{c,rig}(X)).

api.name: rigidTrace_finiteEtale
api.statement: For f: Y → X finite étale between smooth affines, Tr_X ∘ Tr_{f,c} = Tr_Y.

api.name: rigidTrace_gysin
api.statement: For a closed immersion Z' → X' of smooth quasi-projective W-schemes of codimension r lifting Z → X, Tr_X ∘ G_{Z'/X',c} = Tr_Z on H^{2(n−r)}_{c,rig}(Z).

api.name: rigidTrace_crystalline
api.statement: For X proper and smooth, under H^{2n}_{c,rig}(X) = H^{2n}_{rig}(X) ≅ H^{2n}_{crys}(X/W) ⊗ K, Tr_X is the crystalline trace.

api.name: rigidTrace_baseChange
api.statement: For a finite extension K'/K with residue field k', Tr_{X_{k'}} is the K'-linear extension of Tr_X.

api.name: rigidTrace_isIso_of_geomIrreducible

tests.name: rigidTrace_affineLine

nodes.title: Compact-support Gysin maps and their compatibility with the lift-dependent traces
nodes.statement: Let i': Z' → X' be a closed immersion of codimension r between smooth quasi-projective W-schemes with reduction i: Z → X, n = dim X. The algebraic Gysin morphism of i', analytified on the generic fibres and followed by RΓ_{]X[}, gives a compact-support Gysin morphism G_{Z'/X',c}: RΓ_{c,rig}(Z) → RΓ_{c,rig}(X)[2r], natural for open restriction. If X and Z are affine, smooth and geometrically connected and Tr_{X'}, Tr_{Z'} denote the traces built from the lifts as in Berthelot 1.2 (before independence of the lift is known), then Tr_{X'} ∘ G_{Z'/X',c} = Tr_{Z'} on H^{2(n−r)}_{c,rig}(Z). For a W-section Y' ⊂ X' this gives Tr_{X'} ∘ G_{Y'/X',c} = id_K, and the Gysin map of a section is computed in local coordinates near the section by the same formula for any two lifts whose formal completions are identified.
hypotheses: Smooth quasi-projective lifts (affine shrinking as in RD.4/gysin-isomorphism).
proofSteps: Berthelot 1.3: the algebraic Gysin morphism of a closed immersion of smooth schemes is compatible with Grothendieck's traces (the residue formalism of Hartshorne, Residues and Duality, applied on compactifications); analytify, use GAGA for the coherent dualising complexes, and apply RΓ_{]X[}.
Section case: Z' = Y' = Spec W, r = n, Tr_{Y'} is the identity of K.

Local formula: near the section, the tube is a polydisc and G_{Y'/X',c}(1) is the class of the form with residue 1 at the origin of the coordinates (Berthelot 1.6), which only depends on the formal completion along the section.
acceptance: For the zero section of A^1 ⊂ P^1_W, G_c(1) is the class of the form with residue 1, and Tr(G_c(1)) = 1.
For Z = X (r = 0), G is the identity.

nodes.title: Top compact-support cohomology of a geometrically irreducible variety is one-dimensional
nodes.statement: Let X be a separated, geometrically irreducible k-scheme of finite type of dimension n. Then dim_K H^{2n}_{c,rig}(X/K) = 1, and for every open dense U ⊂ X the map H^{2n}_{c,rig}(U) → H^{2n}_{c,rig}(X) is an isomorphism.
hypotheses: Constant coefficients; no Frobenius statement (the Frobenius twist is RD.5/top-compact-support-cohomology, which uses the trace).
proofSteps: Isomorphism for U ⊂ X: excision (RD.4/excision-sequence) with the vanishing of H^d_{c,rig} above twice the dimension of X \ U (RD.5/compact-support-vanishing-above-twice-dimension).

Lower bound: after a finite extension of k (RD.4/finite-flat-base-change) shrink X to a smooth affine with a W-point on a lift; the Gysin map of the point is nonzero since its composite with the lift-dependent trace is the identity (RD.5/compact-support-gysin-and-trace).

Upper bound: shrink X to U finite étale over A^n (RD.3/etale-cover-of-affine-space); then H^{2n}_{c,rig}(A^n, f_*O) is dual to H^0_rig(A^n, f_*O^∨) = H^0_rig(U) = K by RD.5/poincare-duality-on-affine-space, after arranging finiteness and separatedness as in Kedlaya's proof of Lemma 9.3.2 (RD.5/generic-pushforward-theorem, RD.5/strictness-of-vertical-connection, RD.5/strictness-from-finite-cohomology).
acceptance: For X = A^n the dimension is 1 (RD.4/compactly-supported-cohomology-of-affine-space).
For X = Spec(k × k) (not geometrically irreducible, n = 0) the dimension is 2, so geometric irreducibility is needed.

sources.match: States that top compact-support cohomology of a geometrically irreducible variety is one-dimensional, with the lower bound from the Gysin map of a section.
Proves the same dimension statement by finite étale pushforward to affine space and duality on affine space.

nodes.title: Traces along finite étale maps and the averaging projector
nodes.statement: Let f: Y → X be finite étale of degree d between smooth affine k-schemes. A finite étale lift Ã → B̃ of the dagger algebras (unique up to isomorphism) gives traces Tr_f: RΓ_rig(Y) → RΓ_rig(X) and Tr_{f,c}: RΓ_{c,rig}(Y) → RΓ_{c,rig}(X) (the latter through a finite étale map of strict neighbourhoods of the tubes). Then Tr_f ∘ f^* = d and Tr_{f,c} ∘ f^*_c = d, so (1/d)f^*∘Tr_f and (1/d)f^*_c∘Tr_{f,c} are idempotents exhibiting RΓ_rig(X) and RΓ_{c,rig}(X) as direct summands of RΓ_rig(Y) and RΓ_{c,rig}(Y); and Tr_X ∘ Tr_{f,c} = Tr_Y in top degree.
hypotheses: Characteristic of K is 0, so division by d is allowed.
Smooth affine X, Y; the finite étale lift exists by the lifting of étale algebras to weak completions.
proofSteps: Lift f to a finite étale map of dagger algebras (Berthelot 1.4; van der Put); Tr_f is induced by the de Rham trace RD.4/de-rham-trace through the Monsky–Washnitzer comparison RD.4/monsky-washnitzer-comparison.
The finite étale map extends to strict neighbourhoods of the tubes; pushforward of RΓ_{]Y[} gives Tr_{f,c} (Berthelot 1.4).
Tr ∘ f^* is multiplication by the degree on functions, hence on de Rham complexes; compatibility with Tr_X by the projection formula for Grothendieck traces (Berthelot 1.7 (ii)).
acceptance: For the Kummer cover t ↦ t^d of G_m with p ∤ d, (1/d)Tr_f is the projection of H^1_rig onto the invariants, and both H^1 are K·dt/t.

nodes.title: The duality morphism ψ_{Z,X} and its morphism of distinguished triangles
nodes.statement: Let X be a separated k-scheme of finite type of pure dimension n, Z ⊂ X closed with complement U, and E ∈ F-Isoc†(X/K). The cup product RΓ_{Z,rig}(X, E) ⊗_K RΓ_{c,rig}(Z, E^∨) → RΓ_{c,rig}(X, O), built on a frame from RD.5/overconvergent-germ-hom-lemma and a multiplicative injective resolution of the de Rham complex, composed with the trace RD.5/rigid-trace-morphism, gives the duality morphism ψ_{Z,X}: RΓ_{Z,rig}(X, E) → RHom_K(RΓ_{c,rig}(Z, E^∨), K)[−2n] (ψ_X when Z = X). The triple (ψ_{Z,X}, ψ_X, ψ_U) is a morphism from the localisation triangle RΓ_{Z,rig}(X) → RΓ_rig(X) → RΓ_rig(U) → to the K-dual of the excision triangle RΓ_{c,rig}(U) → RΓ_{c,rig}(X) → RΓ_{c,rig}(Z) →, shifted by −2n. It is independent of the choices and satisfies: (i) for X proper smooth, ψ_X is crystalline Poincaré duality; (ii) for f: Y → X finite étale between smooth affines, ψ_X ∘ Tr_f = (f^*)^∨ ∘ ψ_Y and ψ_Y ∘ f^* = (Tr_{f,c})^∨ ∘ ψ_X; (iii) under the hypotheses of RD.5/compact-support-gysin-and-trace, ψ_{Z,X} ∘ G_{Z'/X'} = ψ_Z.
hypotheses: Pure dimension n (the shift −2n and the trace need it).

Coefficients: E ∈ F-Isoc†(X/K) with dual E^∨; Berthelot treats E = O, and the construction is the same for any locally free coefficient since only the pairing E ⊗ E^∨ → O is added (Kedlaya, Section 8.2).
proofSteps: On a frame (X, X̄, P): RΓ_{Z,rig}(X) is computed by the simple complex of j†_X(Ω) → j†_U(Ω), and RΓ_{c,rig}(Z) by Γ_{]Z[} of an injective resolution; RD.5/overconvergent-germ-hom-lemma turns the multiplication of a multiplicative resolution into the pairing into Γ_{]X[} (Berthelot 2.1–2.2).
Compose with Tr_X on H^{2n}_{c,rig}(X) (RD.5/rigid-trace-morphism); vanishing above 2n (RD.5/compact-support-vanishing-above-twice-dimension) makes the composite a map into the shifted dual.
The morphism of triangles comes from the compatibility of the pairing with the maps j†_X → j†_U and Γ_{]U[} → Γ_{]X[} at the level of complexes (Berthelot (2.2.2)).

(i) via the crystalline comparison for proper smooth X (RD.7 owns that comparison; here only the identification of traces from RD.5/rigid-trace-morphism API rigidTrace_crystalline is used); (ii) from RD.5/finite-etale-trace-projector and the projection formula; (iii) from RD.5/compact-support-gysin-and-trace (a).
acceptance: For Z = X = A^1 and E = O, ψ_X in degree 1 identifies H^1_rig(A^1) = 0 with the dual of H^1_{c,rig}(A^1) = 0, and in degree 0 K with the dual of H^2_{c,rig}(A^1) via the trace.

For X = G_m, Z = {1}, U = X \ Z, the triangle morphism matches the localisation sequence 0 → H^1_rig(G_m) → H^1_rig(U) → H^2_{Z,rig}(G_m) ≅ K(−1) → 0 with the dual of the excision sequence 0 → H^0_{c,rig}(Z) → H^1_{c,rig}(U) → H^1_{c,rig}(G_m) → 0.

nodes.title: Künneth pairings on product tubes and the Künneth morphisms with supports
nodes.statement: For i = 1, 2 let X_i be separated k-schemes of finite type with closed Z_i ⊂ X_i, compactifications X̄_i, closed immersions X̄_i ⊂ P_i into formal W-schemes smooth near X_i, projections p_i: ]X̄_1 × X̄_2[ → ]X̄_i[, and sheaves E_i of K-vector spaces on ]X̄_i[. There are canonical pairings p_1^{-1}Γ†_{]Z_1[}(E_1) ⊗_K p_2^{-1}Γ†_{]Z_2[}(E_2) → Γ†_{]Z_1×Z_2[}(p_1^{-1}E_1 ⊗ p_2^{-1}E_2) and p_1^{-1}Γ_{]X_1[}(E_1) ⊗_K p_2^{-1}Γ_{]X_2[}(E_2) → Γ_{]X_1×X_2[}(p_1^{-1}E_1 ⊗ p_2^{-1}E_2). Applied to the de Rham complexes of E_i ∈ F-Isoc†(X_i/K) and the external wedge product, they induce the Künneth morphisms RΓ_{Z_1,rig}(X_1, E_1) ⊗_K RΓ_{Z_2,rig}(X_2, E_2) → RΓ_{Z_1×Z_2,rig}(X_1 × X_2, E_1 ⊠ E_2) and RΓ_{c,rig}(X_1, E_1) ⊗_K RΓ_{c,rig}(X_2, E_2) → RΓ_{c,rig}(X_1 × X_2, E_1 ⊠ E_2), compatible with functoriality and Frobenius, and for fixed X_2 they are morphisms of triangles from (localisation triangle of (X_1, Z_1)) ⊗ RΓ_rig(X_2) to the localisation triangle of (X_1 × X_2, Z_1 × X_2), and likewise for excision triangles with compact supports. Properties: (i) for proper smooth X_i and Z_i = X_i they are the crystalline Künneth maps; (ii) they commute with Tr_{f_1} ⊗ Tr_{f_2} = Tr_{f_1×f_2} (and the compact-support traces) for finite étale covers of smooth affines; (iii) they commute with Gysin maps G_{Z'_1/X'_1} ⊗ G_{Z'_2/X'_2} = G_{Z'_1×Z'_2/X'_1×X'_2}.
hypotheses: Products of frames: ]X̄_1 × X̄_2[ = ]X̄_1[ × ]X̄_2[ and products of strict neighbourhoods are cofinal (RD.3/strict-neighbourhood); Γ†_{]Z[} denotes the kernel of j†_X → j†_U.
proofSteps: The pairings on sheaves: for germs of sections of E_i on strict neighbourhoods, the external product is a germ on the product neighbourhood; supports multiply because ]Z_1 × Z_2[ = ]Z_1[ × ]Z_2[ (Berthelot 3.1).

Apply to multiplicative resolutions of the de Rham complexes and take global sections; the Künneth map of tensor products of complexes of K-vector spaces gives the morphisms (Berthelot (3.1.1)–(3.1.2)).
Compatibility with triangles (Berthelot (3.1.3)–(3.1.4)) is compatibility at the level of complexes with j†_{X_1} → j†_{U_1} and Γ_{]U_1[} → Γ_{]X_1[}.
(i)–(iii): Berthelot 3.3, from RD.5/finite-etale-trace-projector, RD.5/compact-support-gysin-and-trace and the crystalline comparison of traces.
acceptance: For X_1 = X_2 = A^1 with E_i = O, the compact-support Künneth map sends Tr-dual generators of H^2_{c,rig}(A^1) ⊗ H^2_{c,rig}(A^1) to the generator of H^4_{c,rig}(A^2).
For X_2 = Spec k the morphisms are the identity.

nodes.title: Rigid cohomology commutes with arbitrary extension of the base field
nodes.statement: Let k ⊂ k' be an arbitrary extension of fields of characteristic p, with Cohen rings W → W' and K → K' (complete discretely valued, residue fields k, k'). For a separated k-scheme X of finite type, the natural maps H^i_rig(X/K) ⊗_K K' → H^i_rig(X_{k'}/K') and H^i_{c,rig}(X/K) ⊗_K K' → H^i_{c,rig}(X_{k'}/K') are isomorphisms for all i.
hypotheses: Constant coefficients, as in Berthelot's remark; for finite extensions and coefficients see RD.4/finite-flat-base-change.
Both sides are finite dimensional (RD.5/finiteness-of-rigid-cohomology, RD.5/finiteness-of-compactly-supported-rigid-cohomology).
proofSteps: Double induction on dimension exactly as for duality and Künneth (Berthelot Remarque after 3.4): (a)_n for smooth X of dimension ≤ n, (b)_n for cohomology with supports in Z of dimension ≤ n inside smooth X, using the localisation and excision triangles (RD.4/localisation-sequence, RD.4/excision-sequence), Gysin maps for liftable smooth pairs (RD.4/gysin-isomorphism), the proper smooth case through the crystalline comparison, and de Jong's alterations with the finite étale trace projector to pass from opens of proper smooth schemes to general smooth X (RD.5/finite-etale-trace-projector, SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4/de-jong-alteration-theorem).
Proper smooth case: crystalline cohomology commutes with flat base change of the Cohen ring.
Compact supports from the result for H_rig by Poincaré duality on smooth strata and excision.
acceptance: For X = G_m both sides are K' in degrees 0 and 1.
For X = P^1 the map identifies the classes of the hyperplane in degree 2.

sources.match: States that the method of the duality and Künneth inductions proves that rigid cohomology commutes with an arbitrary extension of the base field.
The double induction (a)_n, (b)_n with de Jong's theorem and the finite étale projector that the remark refers to.

nodes.title: Lifting a smooth projective curve with its boundary points, and the algebraic generic fibre
nodes.statement: Let K be complete discretely valued of characteristic 0 with ring of integers O and residue field k, X̄ a smooth projective geometrically irreducible curve over k of genus g, and D = {x_1, …, x_m} ⊂ X̄ a reduced divisor whose points have residue fields k_i separable over k; X = X̄ \ D. Then there are a smooth projective O-curve 𝒳̄ with special fibre X̄ and closed subschemes 𝒟_i ≅ Spec O_{K_i} (K_i/K unramified with residue field k_i) lifting x_i. Moreover: (a) 𝒳 = 𝒳̄ \ ∪𝒟_i is a smooth affine O-scheme lifting X, and its weak completion tensored with K is a dagger algebra A of Monsky–Washnitzer type with special fibre X, unique up to non-canonical isomorphism; (b) the generic fibre C = 𝒳̄_K is a smooth projective geometrically connected K-curve of genus g, so dim_K H^0(C, O) = 1, dim_K H^1(C, O) = g, dim_K H^0(C, Ω^1) = g, dim_K H^1(C, Ω^1) = 1; (c) the analytification C^an is a proper rigid curve containing the tube ]X[ as the complement of the residue discs ]x_i[, each an open disc over K_i.
hypotheses: Separability of the residue fields of the boundary points (Kedlaya's Hypothesis 6.2.1); otherwise first pass to a finite extension of k, which is harmless for dimensions (RD.4/finite-flat-base-change).
Characteristic 0 for K; O need not be the Witt vectors when k is imperfect (a Cohen ring suffices).
proofSteps: Formal lift: obstructions to lifting a smooth curve over O/π^n to O/π^{n+1} lie in H^2(X̄, T_X̄) = 0, and the points lift by smoothness of the curve at x_i (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4/deformations-of-smooth-schemes).

Algebraise the formal curve with its sections (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4/effective-formal-deformations-of-curves, SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4/grothendieck-algebraization); the lift of an ample divisor makes the formal curve projective.

(a) Removing a relatively ample divisor gives an affine smooth lift; its weak completion is of MW type and unique up to isomorphism by the lifting property of weakly complete algebras (AdicSpacesPartII:F1/mw-type-integral-lift, AdicSpacesPartII:F1/weak-completion).

(b) The Euler characteristic of O is locally constant in the flat proper family, H^0 is the constants on both fibres (geometric connectedness), hence h^1 = g; Serre duality on C gives the Ω^1 dimensions (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2/serre-proper).

(c) Raynaud's generic fibre of the completion of 𝒳̄ is C^an (proper GAGA, AdicSpacesPartII:R3/proper-gaga); the tube of x_i is an open disc in a local parameter lifting a uniformiser at x_i (Crew 7.2).
acceptance: For X = A^1 = P^1 \ {∞}, the lift P^1_O with the section ∞ gives A = K⟨t⟩†, C = P^1_K, g = 0.
For an elliptic curve minus its origin, the lift is a Weierstrass model with good reduction and the zero section; g = 1.

sources.match: Sets the curve, its boundary with geometrically reduced points, and Crew's geometric description of the local algebras through a formally smooth lift.
Attaches to each boundary point a local algebra through a lifting of the compactified curve and embeds the dagger algebra into the sum of the local algebras.
Uses the algebraisation of the analytic proper curve as a smooth projective K-curve.

nodes.title: Mayer–Vietoris sequences for a dagger curve and its boundary discs
nodes.statement: In the situation of RD.5/curve-lift-with-boundary, let A(x_i) be the local algebra (Robba ring over K_i in a parameter t_i at x_i) and A(x_i)^+ its subring of functions on the open disc ]x_i[. For every locally free coherent sheaf 𝓛 on C, with L† = colim_V Γ(V, 𝓛^an) over strict neighbourhoods V of ]X[, there is an exact sequence 0 → H^0(C, 𝓛) → L† ⊕ ⊕_i Γ(]x_i[, 𝓛^an) → ⊕_i L† ⊗ A(x_i) → H^1(C, 𝓛) → 0. In particular, writing ρ: A → ⊕_i A(x_i)/A(x_i)^+ and dρ: Ω^1_A → ⊕_i Ω^1_{A(x_i)}/Ω^1_{A(x_i)^+} for the principal-part maps, there are exact sequences 0 → H^0(C, O) → A → ⊕_i A(x_i)/A(x_i)^+ → H^1(C, O) → 0 and 0 → H^0(C, Ω^1) → Ω^1_A → ⊕_i Ω^1_{A(x_i)}/Ω^1_{A(x_i)^+} → H^1(C, Ω^1) → 0.
hypotheses: Locally free coherent 𝓛 on the algebraic curve C (algebraisation via proper GAGA).
Strict neighbourhoods V_r = C^an \ ∪_i {|t_i| < r} for r → 1^−, r ∈ √|K^×|.
proofSteps: For r close to 1, {V_r, [D]_r} with [D]_r = ∪_i{|t_i| < r'} (r < r' < 1, closed discs) is an admissible affinoid covering of C^an, so the Čech complex Γ(V_r) ⊕ Γ([D]_r) → Γ(V_r ∩ [D]_r) computes H^*(C^an, 𝓛^an) (Tate acyclicity, AdicSpacesPartII:R3/tate-kiehl-affinoid; Crew, proof of Theorem 7.5).
H^*(C^an, 𝓛^an) = H^*(C, 𝓛) by proper GAGA (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/proper-gaga).

Pass to the limit r' → 1 (Mittag-Leffler: the transition maps have dense image, AdicSpacesPartII:R3/quasi-stein-dense-restriction) to replace the closed discs by the open discs ]x_i[, then the direct limit over strict neighbourhoods (exact); the intersections become the local algebras (Crew (7.3.3)).
For 𝓛 = O and 𝓛 = Ω^1, eliminating the disc terms gives the four-term sequences, the kernel of ρ being A ∩ ⊕A(x_i)^+ = H^0(C, O).
acceptance: For X = A^1 (C = P^1, one boundary point): 0 → K → K⟨t⟩† → A(∞)/A(∞)^+ → 0 → 0, i.e. ρ is surjective with kernel the constants.
For X = A^1 and Ω^1: H^0(P^1, Ω^1) = 0 and H^1(P^1, Ω^1) = K, so dρ has one-dimensional cokernel, spanned by the class of dt/t at ∞ (the residue).

sources.match: Computes H^*(X^an, L) by the Čech complex of the admissible affinoid cover by a strict neighbourhood and small closed discs at the boundary, then passes to the limit to the open discs and the local algebras.
Defines the sum of local algebras at the boundary and identifies the tensor products of the global module with it as limits over strict neighbourhoods.
Crew's geometric description of the local algebras as overconvergent functions on annuli near the boundary discs.

nodes.title: The indices of the principal-part maps and the dimension of H^1 of an affine curve
nodes.statement: Under Hypothesis 6.2.1 of Kedlaya (X smooth affine geometrically irreducible curve over k, boundary D of degree d = Σ_i [k_i : k], compactification of genus g), the principal-part maps ρ: A → ⊕_i A(x_i)/A(x_i)^+ and dρ: Ω^1_A → ⊕_i Ω^1_{A(x_i)}/Ω^1_{A(x_i)^+} have finite-dimensional kernels and cokernels with ind(ρ) = 1 − g and ind(dρ) = g − 1 (ind = dim ker − dim coker over K), and the local derivative d_loc: ⊕ A(x_i)/A(x_i)^+ → ⊕ Ω^1_{A(x_i)}/Ω^1_{A(x_i)^+} is injective with cokernel ⊕_i K_i · dt_i/t_i, so ind(d_loc) = −d. Consequently ind(d: A → Ω^1_A) = 2 − 2g − d, and since H^0_rig(X/K) = K, dim_K H^1_rig(X/K) = 2g + d − 1.
hypotheses: Hypothesis 6.2.1 (geometrically reduced boundary points); the general case reduces to it by a finite extension of k.
proofSteps: Indices of ρ and dρ: read off the exact sequences of RD.5/dagger-curve-mayer-vietoris with the dimensions of RD.5/curve-lift-with-boundary (b): ind(ρ) = h^0(O) − h^1(O) = 1 − g and ind(dρ) = h^0(Ω^1) − h^1(Ω^1) = g − 1. This replaces the lattice argument on the special fibre that Kedlaya leaves to the reader.

Local derivative: on A(x_i)/A(x_i)^+, represented by series Σ_{n≥1} a_n t^{−n}, d is injective in characteristic 0 and its image misses exactly the class of t^{−1}dt; the coefficient field of the i-th summand is K_i, of degree [k_i : k] over K.
Index additivity for the commutative square d_loc ∘ ρ = dρ ∘ d of maps with finite-dimensional kernels and cokernels (RD.5/near-isomorphism): ind(d) + ind(dρ) = ind(ρ) + ind(d_loc).
H^0 = K for geometrically connected X (Kedlaya, proof of Lemma 9.3.2), and H^1_rig = coker d by RD.4/mw-comparison-for-affine-curves.
acceptance: X = P^1 minus N rational points: dim H^1 = N − 1, matching RD.5/affine-curve-duality-acceptance (1).

sources.locator: Proposition 6.2.10 and the sentence after it, p. 39
sources.match: Proves finiteness from the square of principal-part maps and states, without proof, that more care gives dim H^1 = 2g + deg(boundary) − 1.
States the dimension formula for H^1 of an affine curve.
The Čech computation on the analytic proper curve that yields the exact sequences used here.

nodes.title: Kedlaya's finite projections to projective space étale off the hyperplane at infinity
nodes.statement: Let k be a field of characteristic p > 0, X a geometrically reduced projective k-scheme of pure dimension n with an ample line bundle L, D ⊂ X a closed subscheme of dimension < n, and S a zero-dimensional subscheme of the smooth locus of X not meeting D. Then there is a finite morphism f: X → P^n_k given by n + 1 sections of some power of L, étale away from the hyperplane H at infinity, with f(D) ⊆ H and f(S) ∩ H = ∅. If moreover D_1, …, D_m are irreducible divisors meeting transversely at a smooth point x, one can take an open dense U ∋ x with a finite étale map U → A^n sending the D_j into coordinate hyperplanes.
hypotheses: Geometric reducedness is necessary: a scheme with a generically étale map to a smooth scheme has generically smooth components.
Finite fields are allowed: the sections are produced by powers 'sufficiently divisible' rather than by generic choice.
proofSteps: Lemma 3: n + 1 sections of an ample bundle without common zero define a finite map to P^n (fibres are both affine and proper).
Lemma 4: for l sufficiently divisible there is a section of L^l vanishing on D but not at any point of a given finite subscheme Z (complement of a section is affine).
Lemma 5: inductively choose sections s_1, …, s_n vanishing on S (and along D_i) whose zero loci cut D in the expected codimension, so that they have no common zero on D.

Lemma 6: with α a section with zero locus D and functions f_i = β_i/α^{j_i} giving a map unramified at S, the sections δ_i = β_i α^{l−2j_i} + γ_i^2, with γ_i vanishing on S, define a finite map unramified at S, since the squares have zero differential along S.

Theorem 1: let g be the finite map from s^m, s_1, …, s_n given by Lemma 6, unramified at S, and E the closed locus of X \ D where g ramifies; choose t vanishing on E but not on S (Lemma 4) and t_1, …, t_n without common zero on the zero locus Z of t (Lemma 5), and put u_0 = t^{pl}, u_i = s_i s^{m(pr−1)} t^{p(l−1)} + t_i^p. In characteristic p the p-th powers t_i^p have zero differential, so off Z the differentials of u_i/u_0 are those of s_i/s^m times the unit (s^{rm}/t)^p; hence the finite map f = (u_0 : … : u_n) (Lemma 3) is étale off the hyperplane u_0 = 0, which contains f(D) and misses f(S).

Theorem 2: replace X by a projective compactification of an affine neighbourhood of x, blow up away from x so that all intersections of the D_i are irreducible, and run the proof of Theorem 1 with S = {x} and s_i, t_i vanishing along D_i; restrict to the preimage of A^n = P^n \ H.
acceptance: For X = P^1 and D = {∞}, f can be taken to be the identity.

Non-example of the naive choice: for E: y^2 = x^3 + ax + b over F_q (p odd) and D = {O}, the coordinate x: E → P^1 is finite with f(D) = ∞ but ramified over the three roots of the cubic in A^1, so it is not étale off ∞; the theorem replaces it by sections of a higher power of O(O) modified by p-th powers.

sources.match: States the finite projection to projective space étale off the hyperplane at infinity with prescribed behaviour on D and S, and the affine refinement with transverse divisors.
Builds the étale-off-the-hyperplane map from the unramified map of Lemma 6 by adding p-th powers, and handles transverse divisors by blowing up away from the point.
Noether normalisation lemmas with sections of powers of an ample bundle, valid over finite fields, and the construction of a map unramified at the chosen points.
The form used in the finiteness proof: an open dense affine around a smooth point, finite étale over affine space.

nodes.title: Log-rigid cohomology of a curve with unipotent monodromy equals rigid cohomology of the complement
nodes.statement: Let Y be a smooth curve over a perfect field k, Z ⊂ Y a finite set of k-rational points, and E ∈ F-Isoc†(Y \ Z/K) with unipotent monodromy along Z, with log extension E^log (a convergent log-F-isocrystal on (Y, Z) with nilpotent residues N_z, RD.5/log-extension-of-unipotent-isocrystal). Define the log-rigid cohomology H^i_{log-rig}((Y, Z)/K, E^log) as the hypercohomology of the overconvergent log de Rham complex E^log ⊗ Ω^•(log Z) on the tube of Y. Then the restriction map H^i_{log-rig}((Y, Z)/K, E^log) → H^i_rig(Y \ Z/K, E) is a Frobenius-compatible isomorphism for every i; in particular the log-rigid cohomology is finite dimensional.
hypotheses: Unipotent monodromy along Z; without it the log extension with nilpotent residues does not exist, and for residues with nonzero integer eigenvalues the comparison fails.
Rational points of Z (otherwise pass to a finite extension of k; RD.4/finite-flat-base-change).
proofSteps: Cover the tube of Y by a strict neighbourhood U_1 of the tube of Y \ Z and the residue discs U_2 = ⊔_z ]z[; U_1 ∩ U_2 is a union of annulus germs at the boundaries of the discs. The Mayer–Vietoris sequence for the log de Rham complex reads … → H^i_{log-rig}(Y) → H^i(U_1, E) ⊕ H^i_log(U_2, E^log) → H^i(U_1 ∩ U_2, E) → …, and H^*(U_1, E) = H^*_rig(Y \ Z, E) (RD.4/overconvergent-de-rham-complex).

On a residue disc, E^log is isomorphic to a constant module with log connection d + N_z dt/t (Kedlaya, Semistable reduction I, Theorem 3.3.4, the logarithmic form of RD.2/unipotent-iff-nilpotent-residue); for n ≥ 1 the operator n + N_z is invertible, so H^0_log = ker N_z and H^1_log = coker N_z, coming from the t^0 terms (antiderivatives, RD.2/robba-ring-antiderivative).

On an annulus germ (the Robba ring), the same constant form gives H^0 = ker N_z and H^1 = coker N_z, since n + N_z is invertible for every n ≠ 0 (RD.5/unipotent-local-residue-isomorphism); the restriction from the disc is an isomorphism on these t^0 terms.

Hence the disc terms cancel the annulus terms in the Mayer–Vietoris sequence, and restriction to U_1 is an isomorphism; finiteness follows from RD.5/finiteness-for-affine-curves (Y \ Z affine) or RD.5/finiteness-of-rigid-cohomology.
acceptance: Y = A^1, Z = {0}, E = O: the log complex K⟨t⟩† → K⟨t⟩† dt/t has H^0 = K and H^1 = K·dt/t, which is H^*_rig(G_m), not H^*_rig(A^1) = (K, 0): log cohomology of (A^1, {0}) is the cohomology of the complement.
Y = A^1, Z = {0}, E of rank two with ∇ = d + N dt/t, N a nonzero nilpotent 2 × 2 matrix: H^0 = ker N = K and H^1 = coker N = K on both sides.

Non-example: the rank-one log connection d + dt/t (residue 1, not nilpotent) on (A^1, {0}) has log-rigid cohomology 0 in both degrees (t^n ↦ (n + 1)t^n dt/t is bijective for n ≥ 0), while its restriction to G_m is isomorphic to O via multiplication by t, with cohomology (K, K); residues with integer eigenvalues other than 0 must be excluded.

sources.match: Identifies the Igusa theta-cokernel with log-rigid cohomology of a log F-isocrystal on compactified Igusa curves and deduces finiteness from general finiteness of rigid cohomology.

The functor U_I, which equips the pullback of a module on the base with the connection twisted by commuting nilpotent residues N_i dt_i/t_i, is an equivalence onto unipotent log-∇-modules on the base times a polyannulus or polydisc.
Unipotent monodromy along a strict normal crossings divisor is equivalent to a convergent log-isocrystal extension with nilpotent residues, and the extension is unique.
Finite dimensionality on curves via the local unipotent computation at the missing points.

nodes.title: Acceptance: finite-level Igusa rigid cohomology with Sym^k coefficients is finite dimensional
nodes.statement: For k ≥ 0, n ≥ 0 and tame level K^p, the space H^1_rig(Ig(K^pΓ(p^n)), Sym^k) of Pan, Definition 5.1.6 (the cokernel of θ^{k+1}: M†_{−k} → M†_{k+2} ⊗ D_0^{−k−1} at level K^pΓ(p^n)), once identified at RD.4 with the log-rigid cohomology of the ordinary locus of the compactified Igusa curves at that level, with log poles at the cusps and coefficients Sym^k of the log-F-isocrystal H^1 of the universal generalised elliptic curve, is finite dimensional.
hypotheses: The identification of the theta-cokernel with log-rigid cohomology is an RD.4 target (Pan Definition 5.1.6, after Coleman); this node only proves finiteness.

The overconvergence of R^1f_*O of the universal ordinary elliptic curve along the supersingular points and its unipotent (Tate curve) monodromy at the cusps are RD.3 inputs (Étesse's overconvergence of abelian-scheme direct images).
Igusa curves at level K^pΓ(p^n) in characteristic p are the Igusa components of ModularCurvesPartII:R13.5/igusa-components.
proofSteps: Sym^k H^1 is an overconvergent F-isocrystal on the ordinary locus minus the cusps with unipotent monodromy at the cusps, hence log-extendable with nilpotent residues (RD.5/log-extension-of-unipotent-isocrystal).

By RD.5/log-rigid-comparison-for-curves the log-rigid cohomology is H^1_rig of the ordinary locus minus the cusps, a smooth affine curve, which is finite dimensional (RD.5/finiteness-for-affine-curves).
acceptance: For k = 0 the space is H^1_rig of the ordinary locus minus the cusps; on a geometrically connected component of genus g with s supersingular and c cuspidal geometric points its dimension is 2g + s + c − 1 (RD.5/dimension-of-h1-of-affine-curve).
The colimit over n is not finite dimensional (Pan Proposition 5.1.8 uses it with a smooth Borel action), so finiteness is a finite-level statement.

sources.match: Defines the theta-cokernel spaces at finite level and in the limit, and proves finite dimensionality at finite level by Coleman's log-rigid interpretation and general finiteness.
Uses the finiteness to get closed images of θ^{k+1} and to describe the cokernel at infinity.

nodes.title: A space that is both Fréchet and the strong dual of a reflexive Fréchet space is finite dimensional
nodes.statement: Let K be discretely valued. If a locally convex K-space V is Fréchet and is (topologically) the strong dual of a reflexive Fréchet space, then dim_K V < ∞.
hypotheses: K discretely valued (hence spherically complete), as throughout Crew's paper.
proofSteps: V has a countable basis of convex neighbourhoods of 0 (Fréchet) and, as the strong dual of a Fréchet space, a countable fundamental family of bounded convex sets B_n (LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L0/bounded-sets-strong-dual).

Choose λ_n with λ_n B_n ⊂ U_n; the closed convex hull of ∪ λ_n B_n is a bounded barrel, hence a neighbourhood of 0 since Fréchet spaces are barrelled (LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L0/barrelled-banach-steinhaus); a space with a bounded neighbourhood of 0 is normable, so V is Banach.

V is reflexive as the dual of a reflexive space; a reflexive Banach space over a discretely valued field is finite dimensional (Crew 2.2; the unit ball of an infinite-dimensional Banach space over a discretely valued field is not weakly compact).
acceptance: K itself is Fréchet and the dual of K.
The Tate algebra K⟨t⟩ is Banach but not reflexive, so not a dual of a reflexive Fréchet space; the space of germs of functions at the boundary, R^−, is dual-of-Fréchet but not Fréchet.

sources.match: A locally convex space that is both Fréchet and dual-of-Fréchet is finite dimensional, by building a bounded barrel and using Kolmogorov's normability criterion and non-reflexivity of infinite-dimensional Banach spaces.

nodes.title: Strictness of a linear map and of its transpose
nodes.statement: Let K be discretely valued and f: V → W a continuous linear map of separated locally convex K-spaces. (a) f is strict iff the image of its transpose f': W' → V' is closed for the weak topology and every equicontinuous subset of im f' is the image of an equicontinuous subset of W'; then ker f' = (im f)^⊥, im f' = (ker f)^⊥, and coker f' ≅ (ker f)' and ker f' ≅ (coker f)' as vector spaces. (b) The transpose of a strict exact sequence is exact. (c) For semi-complete V, W, f' is strict for the linearly-compact dual topologies iff f(V) is closed and every bounded convex linearly compact subset of W is the image of one of V. (d) If V, W are Fréchet, f is strict iff f' is strict for the linearly-compact dual topology; if moreover V, W are Montel (the case of the local algebras), f is strict iff f': W'_b → V'_b is strict.
hypotheses: Equicontinuous may be replaced by bounded for LF-spaces (barrelled).
Spherical completeness of K enters through Hahn–Banach and the bipolar theorem.
proofSteps: (a) The nonarchimedean form of Bourbaki EVT IV §4 no. 1 Prop. 2: the bipolar theorem (LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L0/pseudo-polar-duality) identifies closures with bipolars, and Hahn–Banach (LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L0/nonarchimedean-hahn-banach (b)) extends forms from closed subspaces (Crew 3.8).
(b) A strict exact sequence stays strict exact for the weak topologies; its transpose is exact, the injective case being Hahn–Banach (Crew 3.9).
(c) Mackey: V = (V'_c)' for semi-complete V, and convex equicontinuous subsets of the dual are the relatively linearly compact convex sets (Crew 3.10).

(d) In a Fréchet space every balanced convex closed bounded linearly compact set lies in the closed convex hull of a null sequence (Crew 2.9); lift null sequences along a strict map of metrisable spaces (Crew 3.11); for Montel spaces linearly compact and strong duals agree (Crew 3.12).
acceptance: An isomorphism of Fréchet spaces is strict and so is its transpose.

The inclusion K⟨t⟩† → K⟨t⟩ of overconvergent into convergent functions is continuous but not strict: the topology induced by the Gauss norm on K⟨t⟩† is strictly coarser than its LF (fringe) topology; its image is dense and not closed.

sources.match: Characterises strict maps through their transposes, proves exactness of transposes of strict exact sequences, and treats the Fréchet and Fréchet–Montel cases using linearly compact sets.
Uses the Fréchet–Montel criterion in the duality on affine space.

nodes.title: Topological local duality: the Robba ring is the strong dual of its differentials under the residue pairing
nodes.statement: Let A be the local algebra (the Robba ring of Laurent series in x over a discretely valued K converging on some annulus r < |x| < 1) with its LF topology A = lim_{r→1} A_{(r,1)}, and Ω^1_A = A·dx/x. The residue pairing A × Ω^1_A → K, (f, ω) ↦ Res_{x=0}(fω) (the coefficient of dx/x), is separately continuous and induces topological isomorphisms A ≅ (Ω^1_A)'_b and Ω^1_A ≅ A'_b. A subset of A is bounded iff it lies and is bounded in some A_{[r,1)}, iff its image in (Ω^1_A)'_b is bounded; A is Montel; and for every finite free A-module M the induced map M → (M^∨ ⊗ Ω^1_A)'_b is a topological isomorphism. The pairing satisfies (f, dg) = −(g, df).
hypotheses: K discretely valued; the LF topology of the Robba ring is the RD.0 carrier topology.

This is the topological duality of the coefficient ring itself (Crew 5.4); the perfectness of the cohomological pairing coker ∂ × ker ∂^∨ → L for a module with Frobenius is the distinct RD.1 target RD.1/robba-residue-duality.
proofSteps: Continuity and injectivity: |(f, g dx/x)| ≤ |fg|_I ≤ |f|_I|g|_I on closed annuli I ⊂ (r, 1), and the coefficient functionals (·, x^{n}dx/x) separate points (Crew 5.1).

Surjectivity: a continuous functional ℓ on Ω^1_A is bounded on some U_{ε,[s,t]} for each s < 1; the coefficients a_{−n} = ℓ(x^n dx/x) satisfy the growth conditions (4.1.2)–(4.1.3), hence define f ∈ A with ℓ = (f, ·) (Crew (5.1.5)–(5.1.6)).

Bounded sets (Crew Lemma 5.2) by Banach–Steinhaus on the barrelled space Ω^1_A (LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L0/barrelled-banach-steinhaus); Montel from relative linear compactness of bounded sets, via complete continuity of restriction between nested annuli (Crew Lemma 4.3, Corollary 4.4, Corollary 5.3).

Strictness of A → (Ω^1_A)'_b: A is reflexive (Montel), so this map is its own transpose, and bounded sets correspond (Crew Theorem 5.4 using RD.5/strictness-transpose-criteria); finite free modules reduce to A^n.
acceptance: (1, x^{n} dx/x) = δ_{n,0} for n ∈ ℤ.
(f, df) = 0 for every f (Res d = 0).

sources.match: Defines the local algebras with their LF topology, the residue pairing, proves its continuity and perfectness, characterises bounded sets, and proves that finite free modules are Montel and topologically dual to their twisted duals.

nodes.title: The plus and minus parts of the Robba ring and their mutual duality
nodes.statement: With A and Ω^1_A as in RD.5/robba-topological-residue-duality, let A^+ = A_{[0,1)} (power series converging on the open unit disc), A^− the series with only negative powers of x, Ω^{1,±} = A^± dx. Then A = A^+ ⊕ A^− topologically, (A^+)^⊥ = Ω^{1,+} for the residue pairing, A^+ (with its Fréchet topology, which is the induced one) is Fréchet, A^− is dual-of-Fréchet, and the pairing identifies A^− with the strong dual of the reflexive Fréchet space Ω^{1,+} and (A^+)'_b with Ω^{1,−}.
hypotheses: As in RD.5/robba-topological-residue-duality.
proofSteps: (A^+)^⊥ = Ω^{1,+}: the product of a power series and an element of A^+dx has no x^{−1}dx term, and conversely by testing against x^n (Crew, before 5.5).
Hence A^+ and A^− are closed and A = A^+ ⊕ A^− topologically; A^+ is Fréchet in its own topology, which agrees with the induced one by the open mapping theorem for LF-spaces (Crew 3.5).

Dualise the direct sum with RD.5/robba-topological-residue-duality: A'_b = (A^+)'_b ⊕ (A^−)'_b and (A^+)'_b = Ω^1_A/(A^+)^⊥ ≅ Ω^{1,−}; hence A^− is the dual of the reflexive Fréchet space Ω^{1,+} (Crew Proposition 5.5).
acceptance: The pairing of x^{−n} ∈ A^− with x^{n} dx/x = x^{n−1}dx ∈ Ω^{1,+} (n ≥ 1) is 1.
dA^+ ⊂ Ω^{1,+} and d(A^−) ⊂ Ω^{1,−} with cokernel K·dx/x on the minus side.

sources.locator: Paragraph before Proposition 5.5 and Proposition 5.5, p. 734
sources.match: Shows A = A^+ ⊕ A^− topologically, A^+ Fréchet and A^− dual-of-Fréchet, and identifies the duals through the residue pairing.

nodes.title: Finite rigid and dagger cohomology for smooth quasi-projective integral models and their boundary strata
nodes.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K and residue field k, and 𝒴 a smooth quasi-projective O_K-scheme with special fibre Y and dagger tube 𝒴^† (the dagger space structure on the tube ]Y[ inside the analytification of the generic fibre). (a) H^i_rig(Y/K) is finite dimensional for every i, the Frobenius of RD.4 is bijective on it, and, through the comparison H^i_rig(Y/K) ≅ H^i(𝒴^†, Ω^•) of Grosse-Klönne's Theorem 5.1 (an RD.4 target), the dagger de Rham cohomology of the tube is finite dimensional, functorially in morphisms of smooth quasi-projective models. (b) If 𝒳 is smooth quasi-projective over O_K with a relative strict normal crossings divisor 𝒟 whose strata 𝒟^{(j)} (disjoint unions of j-fold intersections) are smooth quasi-projective, then every first-quadrant spectral sequence with E_1^{i,j} = H^i_rig(D^{(j)}/K), Frobenius-compatible with the induced differentials (such as the boundary-stratum sequence of Harris–Lan–Taylor–Thorne, Lemma 6.21), has finite-dimensional abutment on which the abutting Frobenius is bijective.
hypotheses: Smooth quasi-projective models: the comparison needs the tube of the special fibre inside the generic fibre of the closure in a projective space, not the whole generic fibre (HLTT Lemma 6.8).
Constant coefficients, as in the source; coefficients would need the comparison with coefficients.
proofSteps: (a) Finiteness of H_rig of the separated finite-type k-scheme Y: RD.5/finiteness-of-rigid-cohomology; bijectivity of Frobenius: RD.5/frobenius-bijective-on-cohomology.

The dagger–rigid comparison (Grosse-Klönne Theorem 5.1 (c), applied to the closure of 𝒴 in a projective space, with functoriality as explained in HLTT Lemma 6.8) is planned at RD.4; the finiteness transfers through it.

(b) Each E_1 term is finite dimensional by (a) applied to the strata, only finitely many are nonzero in each total degree (D^{(j)} is empty for j > dim, and H^i_rig vanishes for i > 2 dim), so the abutment is finite dimensional; Frobenius acts compatibly on the filtration with bijective graded pieces, hence bijectively (HLTT Corollary 6.22).
acceptance: 𝒴 = A^n_{O_K}: H^0 = K and the dagger tube is the overconvergent closed polydisc with H^i_dR = 0 for i > 0.
𝒳 = P^1_{O_K} with 𝒟 = {0, ∞}: E_1 has H^*_rig(P^1) and K^2 in the row j = 1, abutment the compactly supported (toward 𝒟) cohomology of G_m, of total dimension 2.

sources.match: For smooth quasi-projective models identifies rigid cohomology of the special fibre with de Rham cohomology of the dagger tube, functorially, via Grosse-Klönne's Theorem 5.1.
Computes the boundary-supported dagger cohomology by a spectral sequence from the rigid cohomology of boundary strata and deduces finite dimensionality from Berthelot's finiteness theorem.

For a proper admissible formal scheme and an immersion of Y into its special fibre, compares coherent and de Rham cohomology of the dagger space on the tube with j†-cohomology, hence with rigid cohomology when the formal scheme is smooth along Y.

nodes.title: Relative convergent cohomology equals rational relative crystalline cohomology, and is perfect
nodes.statement: Let f: (X, M_X) → (Y, M_Y) be a proper log smooth integral morphism of fine log schemes over k, with (Y, M_Y) → (𝒴, M_𝒴) an exact closed immersion into a p-adic formal log scheme defined by p, and E a locally free isocrystal on the relative log convergent site (X/𝒴)^log_conv with associated crystal Φ(E) on the relative log crystalline site. Then the natural map Rf_{X/𝒴,conv*}E → Rf_{X/𝒴,crys*}Φ(E) ⊗ Q is a quasi-isomorphism, and Rf_{X/𝒴,conv*}E is a perfect complex of Q ⊗ O_𝒴-modules. For trivial log structures and a point base this recovers Ogus's comparison of convergent and rational crystalline cohomology.
hypotheses: Proper log smooth integral f; locally free coefficients (crystals in perfect complexes reduce to these by a finite filtration, Guo–Reinecke footnote 13).
proofSteps: Shiho Theorem 2.36: with an embedding into a log smooth formal scheme, both sides are computed by de Rham complexes of the same module, on the log tube and on the p-adically completed log PD envelope; the map is the specialisation map, an isomorphism after reduction to the case where the embedding is an isomorphism; in general use embedding systems.
Perfectness: Shiho Corollary 2.37 from Theorem 2.36 and perfectness of log crystalline cohomology of proper log smooth morphisms (CrystallineCohomology:CR.3/proper-perfectness in the non-log case).
acceptance: For f the identity, both sides are E.
For X → Spec k proper smooth and E = O, this is H^*_conv(X/K) = H^*_crys(X/W)[1/p].

sources.match: Relative log convergent cohomology of a locally free isocrystal is quasi-isomorphic to rational relative log crystalline cohomology and is a perfect complex.
Uses Shiho's Theorem 2.36 and Corollary 2.37 (with Ogus's Theorem 0.7.7 over a point) for perfectness and for the comparison on p-torsion-free PD thickenings.

nodes.title: Higher direct images of convergent F-isocrystals under smooth proper morphisms (Xu)
nodes.statement: Let k be perfect and g: X → Y a smooth proper morphism of k-schemes locally of finite type. For every convergent isocrystal (resp. F-isocrystal) E on X/W, the higher direct images R^ig_{conv*}E are convergent isocrystals (resp. F-isocrystals) on Y/W; the Frobenius structure of R^ig_*E is induced by the natural isomorphism F_Y^*Rg_*E ≅ Rg_*(F_X^*E) composed with the Frobenius of E.
hypotheses: Perfect k; smooth proper g. Neither a lift of Frobenius nor a lift of g is assumed.
proofSteps: Xu Theorem 1.9 (§9.3): Frobenius descent for convergent isocrystals via an Oyama-type site-theoretic Cartier transform (Theorem 1.5 (6.6), Corollary 1.6 (6.7)), comparison of de Rham complexes (Corollary 1.8 (6.9)), and Ogus's description of the direct image of the structure sheaf by relative crystalline cohomology to obtain coherence and convergence.
Frobenius structure: by base change for the Frobenius of Y and the Frobenius of E (Xu Proposition 5.10 and §9.3).
acceptance: For g = id the direct image is E.

For g: E → B an elliptic curve over an ordinary-locus base and E = O, R^1g_*O is the rank-two convergent F-isocrystal of the family, with the unit-root subobject of RD.5/dense-open-restriction-fully-faithful's second acceptance test.

sources.locator: Theorem 1.9, p. 3 (Corollary 9.3, p. 32, in the body)
sources.match: The higher direct image of a convergent isocrystal or F-isocrystal under a smooth proper morphism of k-schemes is a convergent isocrystal or F-isocrystal.
Frobenius descent and the de Rham comparison used in the proof.
Cites Xu's results (published numbering Corollary 8.3, Theorem 3.22) for convergence and the Frobenius structure.

nodes.title: Smooth proper direct images of crystals in perfect complexes underlying F-isocrystals (Guo–Reinecke)
nodes.statement: Let f: Z_1 → Z_2 be a smooth proper morphism of smooth O_K/p-schemes, f_s: Z_{1,s} → Z_{2,s} the induced map of reduced special fibres, and E' a crystal in perfect complexes on Z_{1,crys} underlying an F-isocrystal (E'[1/p], φ_{E'}) after inverting p. (i) Rf_{s,crys*}E'[1/p] underlies a convergent F-isocrystal in perfect complexes on Z_{2,crys}. (ii) For every p-complete p-torsion-free divided power thickening (A, A/J) in Z_{2,crys} there is a natural isomorphism Rf_{s,crys*}E'[1/p](A, A/J) ≅ RΓ((Z_{1,A/J}/A)_crys, E')[1/p], where the left side is the value of the associated convergent crystal of complexes.
hypotheses: Smooth proper f; E' a crystal in perfect complexes (not only a vector bundle); integrality is used only to bound the crystalline cohomology.
Absolute finiteness of rigid cohomology does not imply this relative statement; it is a separate input for consumers working over PD thickenings.
proofSteps: (i) Perfectness of the restriction to p-torsion-free thickenings: RD.5/relative-convergent-crystalline-comparison (Shiho), after filtering E'[1/p] by its cohomology isocrystals; convergence and Frobenius structure: RD.5/convergent-direct-image-smooth-proper (Xu), with φ given by base change.

(ii) On a p-torsion-free PD thickening, the integral crystalline cohomology of the proper smooth Z_{1,A/J} is bounded (CrystallineCohomology:CR.3/proper-perfectness), so rational crystalline equals convergent cohomology there (RD.5/relative-convergent-crystalline-comparison; Ogus over a point).
acceptance: For f = id and E' = O, both sides are A[1/p].
For f a smooth proper curve over a smooth base and E' = O, the value at a p-torsion-free thickening is relative crystalline H^*(Z_1/A)[1/p], of ranks 1, 2g, 1.

sources.match: States and proves that the rational crystalline direct image of a crystal in perfect complexes underlying an F-isocrystal is a convergent F-isocrystal in perfect complexes whose values on p-torsion-free PD thickenings are rational crystalline cohomology.

nodes.title: Constant and unipotent monodromy along a boundary divisor; docile isocrystals
nodes.statement: Let X ⊂ Y be an open immersion of smooth k-varieties with Z = Y \ X, and E an isocrystal on X overconvergent along Z. First, under Kedlaya's Hypothesis 4.3.2 (Y, X affine, Z smooth cut out by f with df a local basis direction, and a small frame), the tube of Z decomposes as ]Z[_Q × A^1_K[0, 1) and E restricts to a ∇-module on ]Z[_Q × A^1_K[λ, 1) for some λ < 1; E has constant (resp. unipotent) monodromy along Z if that restriction is constant (resp. admits an exhaustive filtration with constant quotients) as a log-∇-module relative to ]Z[_Q. In general, E has constant/unipotent monodromy along Z if this holds after every complete extension K'/K (residue field k') for every small frame enclosing an open V ⊂ Y in which V \ X is smooth and principal. When Y is smooth and proper and Z is a strict normal crossings divisor, an isocrystal (or F-isocrystal) on X overconvergent along Z with unipotent monodromy along Z is called docile; Isoc†(X)^doc denotes the full subcategory.
hypotheses: Smooth X and Y; for k perfect it suffices to test on a dense open of each component of Z (Kedlaya Remark 4.4.3).
Monodromy along a divisor is a codimension-one notion: removing a closed subset of codimension ≥ 2 from Y does not change it (Kedlaya Proposition 4.4.4).
proofSteps: Local definition: Kedlaya Lemma 4.3.3 (the tubular decomposition ]Z[_P ≅ ]Z[_Q × A^1[0, 1)) and Definition 4.3.4; constancy and unipotence of log-∇-modules on V × A^n_K(I): Kedlaya Definitions 3.2.5–3.2.6 with the structure theorem 3.3.4 (unipotent modules are U_I of a module with commuting nilpotent residues).

Global definition by testing on all small frames over all field extensions: Kedlaya Definition 4.4.2; independence of choices and Zariski locality: Kedlaya Remark 4.4.1 and the list before Definition 4.4.2.
Docility: D'Addezio Definition 4.4.1 (the same notion for a smooth proper compactification with simple normal crossings boundary).
acceptance: The constant F-isocrystal O_X is docile for every SNC compactification.
The Kummer isocrystal on G_m given by ∇ = d + a dt/t with a ∈ (q − 1)^{−1}ℤ \ ℤ is not docile along {0, ∞}, but its pullback along t ↦ t^{q−1} is.

sources.match: Defines constant and unipotent monodromy along a smooth principal divisor through the tubular decomposition of its tube.
Extends the definition to arbitrary boundaries by testing on all small frames after field extension, and shows its codimension-one nature.
Constant and unipotent log-∇-modules on products with polyannuli, and stability of unipotence under subquotients and tensor products.
Calls an overconvergent isocrystal on the complement of a simple normal crossings divisor in a smooth proper variety docile when it has unipotent monodromy along the divisor.
